bull_bear.body: ₹26 Cr capex funded via conversion of preferential warrants to equity; no new debt raised; focus on internal accruals and subsidiary reinvestment
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in capex execution; agri-equipment demand volatility; dealer network rollout lag; competition from established agri OEMs; macroeconomic slowdown impacting infra spending
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The ₹26 Cr capex is fully funded by warrant conversion — no dilution or debt, making this a low-risk, high-impact growth lever; subsidiaries are not consolidated but contribute meaningfully to revenue and margin expansion
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Growth capital is equity-funded rather than levered: the ₹26 Crore capex draws on a recently completed conversion of preferential warrants to equity, "ensuring no major debt burden for this capex initiative".
- Inorganic step already in the plan: Ganesh Agro Equipment is an "Associate: In process of acquiring 50% through AEML", and the 2031 ambition explicitly contemplates acquisitions and strategic partnerships.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- technology: In-house R&D capabilities cited as a competitive edge in the crushing and screening market — evidence: "Our in-house R&D capabilities and superior manufacturing practices provide a competitive edge."
- cost position: Lower Indian labour costs cited as a manufacturing cost advantage — evidence: "India’s lower labor costs provide a significant competitive advantage in manufacturing, enabling us to offer cost-effective solutions."
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global economic volatility — Fluctuations in the global financial market could impact the Indian economy, potentially leading to a slowdown in demand for crushing and screening equipment.
- Intense competition and pricing pressure — Numerous local players offering low-priced products create price pressure and limit the company's ability to command higher prices; during the year management accepted orders at break-even sales value domestically due to stiff competition.
- Raw material price volatility — Fluctuations in steel and other raw material prices can raise manufacturing costs and affect profit margins.
- Export market concentration and geopolitical exposure — Outside Nepal, the company could not secure expected export orders due to geopolitical conditions and USD-crisis conditions in the countries it exports to, leaving the export market sluggish.
- Rising capital costs and geopolitical uncertainty — Management flagged rising capital costs and uncertainties in the global geopolitical landscape as risks that could impact the outlook.
- Single-segment concentration — The Company operates in a single reportable segment (manufacturing and sale of Construction and Mining Machineries and Spare Parts), concentrating business risk in one industry vertical.
- New-product execution risk in road construction equipment and cranes — Growth is anticipated from as-yet-unproven new product lines (road construction equipment still in development; pick-and-carry cranes at prototype stage with regulatory clearances pending).
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Established 1987 and part of the Gujarat Apollo Group (Mehsana) with "an over 50 years of engineering legacy"; the historical line of business is manufacturing and sales of Construction and Mining equipment.
- Two stated strategic pillars: "LONG STANDING PRESENCE" — "GA is not a new entrant", with confidence in capturing share "derived from decades of operation history and proven reliability" — and "BRAND IMAGE", a favourable image among existing customers.
- Re-entry story: the deck's timeline shows 2013 sale of the Road-construction equipment business to a European MNC (continuing with a 30% stake), 2020 full exit of the remaining 30%, and 2025 "Restarted the development of Road-construction equipment post the end of Non-compete".
- Agri-equipment is framed as diversification: the stream "provides a counter-balance to the heavy infra-equipment, diversifying the group's risk profile."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] AEML Investments Ltd (formerly Apollo Earthmovers Ltd) is a wholly owned subsidiary; Fieldtrack Earthmovers Pvt. Ltd. is a step-down subsidiary "100% held by GA through AEML"; Krishitek Industries Pvt. Ltd. is an "Associate: 50% held by GA through AEML"; Ganesh Agro Equipment Pvt. Ltd. is an associate "In process of acquiring 50% through AEML".
- [Deck scope] The presentation is a forward-looking strategy document filed under Regulation 30 and dated March 12, 2026; it carries no financial statements, order book, market-share or margin data.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells Crushing & Screening equipment along with construction and material handling machinery and spare parts, operating in a single reportable segment. Its equipment serves road construction, building construction, mining and general infrastructure development applications, and it is expanding into road construction equipment and pick-and-carry cranes for material handling.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Crushing and Screening:** Crushing and Screening equipment
- **Construction and material handling:** Road construction equipment (under development), Pick-and-carry cranes (prototype stage)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- AEML Investments Limited (formerly Apollo Earthmovers Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding); manufactures components for agricultural equipment and farm machinery, and is also engaged in real estate projects and trading activities for goods and commodities. Took over Fieldtrack Earthmovers Pvt. Ltd. (FEPL) in FY2025, making it a 100% subsidiary; FEPL manufactures mini tractors (14-25 hp) with a dealer network in Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP and Gujarat.
- Apollo FBC Crushing Equipments Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary; equipment manufacturing (100% shareholding per AOC-1).
- PFH Agri Equipment India Private Limited — associate: Associate held 50% by the company; agriculture and construction equipment manufacturing; yet to commence operations; not consolidated line-by-line (equity method) as it is an associate, not a subsidiary.
- PFH BV — JV: Belgium-based manufacturer of agricultural and construction equipment; joint venture aimed at developing and marketing innovative agricultural machinery solutions; the JV has faced challenges in developing new products. (Note: Directors' Report separately states the Company does not have any Joint Venture.)
- Krishitek Industries Private Limited — related party: Associate of AEML Investments Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary); one director is common. Arm's-length arrangements for purchase of goods/job work/assets/rent/reimbursement during FY2025-26.
- Dev Information Technology Limited — related party: Counterparty where one director is common. Arm's-length arrangements for purchase of goods/job work/assets/rent/reimbursement during FY2025-26.

outlook.body: Pick & Carry Cranes (launching FY26); potential acquisitions in agri-equipment; geographic expansion of dealer network into rural India; possible entry into precision farming tech
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Broadening the portfolio from Crushing and Screening equipment into construction and material handling machinery.
- Developing new road construction machinery product offerings following the expiry of the previous joint venture's non-compete clause.
- Developing pick-and-carry cranes for material handling operations as a long-term expansion domain.
- Prioritising customer service, expanding the distribution network, and investing in marketing and advertising to grow market share in crushing and screening.
- Continuous investment in R&D to maintain innovation standards for new product offerings.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The company is expanding beyond its core Crushing and Screening business into road construction machinery, developing new product offerings for this segment following the expiry of the previous joint venture's non-compete clause. It has also secured technology to manufacture pick-and-carry cranes for material handling; prototype production has commenced along with filings for required regulatory clearances, positioned as a long-term expansion domain.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government emphasis on infrastructure development and mining initiatives is creating robust demand for crushing, screening and construction equipment.
- Rising demand for minerals such as iron ore, coal and copper is stimulating growth in the mining sector and demand for processing equipment.
- Technological advancements in the crushing and screening industry are driving demand for more efficient equipment.
- The crushing and screening market in India is projected to grow, aided by demand from construction, manufacturing and power industries, and government emphasis on infrastructure building is expected to raise demand for road construction equipment.
- Export orders were constrained during the year except to Nepal, due to geopolitical conditions and USD-crisis conditions in other export markets.
- Domestic sales rose because projects previously on hold were awarded amid favourable market conditions, though stiff competition led management to accept orders at break-even sales value for the domestic market.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A crushing and screening equipment manufacturer broadening into road construction machinery and pick-and-carry cranes for the mining, construction and material handling sectors.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells Crushing & Screening equipment along with construction and material handling machinery and spare parts, operating in a single reportable segment. Its equipment serves road construction, building construction, mining and general infrastructure development applications, and it is expanding into road construction equipment and pick-and-carry cranes for material handling.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- AEML Investments Limited (formerly Apollo Earthmovers Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding); manufactures components for agricultural equipment and farm machinery, and is also engaged in real estate projects and trading activities for goods and commodities. Took over Fieldtrack Earthmovers Pvt. Ltd. (FEPL) in FY2025, making it a 100% subsidiary; FEPL manufactures mini tractors (14-25 hp) with a dealer network in Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP and Gujarat.
- Apollo FBC Crushing Equipments Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary; equipment manufacturing (100% shareholding per AOC-1).
- PFH Agri Equipment India Private Limited — associate: Associate held 50% by the company; agriculture and construction equipment manufacturing; yet to commence operations; not consolidated line-by-line (equity method) as it is an associate, not a subsidiary.
- PFH BV — JV: Belgium-based manufacturer of agricultural and construction equipment; joint venture aimed at developing and marketing innovative agricultural machinery solutions; the JV has faced challenges in developing new products. (Note: Directors' Report separately states the Company does not have any Joint Venture.)
- Krishitek Industries Private Limited — related party: Associate of AEML Investments Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary); one director is common. Arm's-length arrangements for purchase of goods/job work/assets/rent/reimbursement during FY2025-26.
- Dev Information Technology Limited — related party: Counterparty where one director is common. Arm's-length arrangements for purchase of goods/job work/assets/rent/reimbursement during FY2025-26.

growth_optionality.body: Pick & Carry Cranes (launching FY26); potential acquisitions in agri-equipment; geographic expansion of dealer network into rural India; possible entry into precision farming tech

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government emphasis on infrastructure development and mining initiatives is creating robust demand for crushing, screening and construction equipment.
- Rising demand for minerals such as iron ore, coal and copper is stimulating growth in the mining sector and demand for processing equipment.
- Technological advancements in the crushing and screening industry are driving demand for more efficient equipment.
- The crushing and screening market in India is projected to grow, aided by demand from construction, manufacturing and power industries, and government emphasis on infrastructure building is expected to raise demand for road construction equipment.
- Export orders were constrained during the year except to Nepal, due to geopolitical conditions and USD-crisis conditions in other export markets.
- Domestic sales rose because projects previously on hold were awarded amid favourable market conditions, though stiff competition led management to accept orders at break-even sales value for the domestic market.

margins.body: Infra equipment margins stable at ~18-20%; agri equipment margins expanding from ~12% to 16-18% due to scale and localized supply chain optimization

capital_allocation.body: ₹26 Cr capex funded via conversion of preferential warrants to equity; no new debt raised; focus on internal accruals and subsidiary reinvestment

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company is expanding beyond its core Crushing and Screening business into road construction machinery, developing new product offerings for this segment following the expiry of the previous joint venture's non-compete clause. It has also secured technology to manufacture pick-and-carry cranes for material handling; prototype production has commenced along with filings for required regulatory clearances, positioned as a long-term expansion domain.

moat.body:

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Broadening the portfolio from Crushing and Screening equipment into construction and material handling machinery.
- Developing new road construction machinery product offerings following the expiry of the previous joint venture's non-compete clause.
- Developing pick-and-carry cranes for material handling operations as a long-term expansion domain.
- Prioritising customer service, expanding the distribution network, and investing in marketing and advertising to grow market share in crushing and screening.
- Continuous investment in R&D to maintain innovation standards for new product offerings.
